assertions.evidence: Section 2.1 defines hallucination rate as a primary evaluation dimension with a detailed 0-10 scoring rubric, severity levels, detection methods (fact-checking, citation verification, confidence calibration), and an automated detection prompt template.

Section 2.2 defines multi-turn coherence as a primary evaluation dimension with a 0-10 scoring rubric covering context reference verification, repetition detection, contradiction detection, and task state tracking.

Section 4.1 specifies 5 runs per test case for initial testing, 5 runs for regression testing (pass rate vs baseline), and 10 runs for quality baseline (mean +/- standard deviation). Total 175 runs across 35 test cases.

All test cases use 'output_properties' with behavioral descriptions like 'does not invent nonexistent payment methods', 'does not fabricate launch timelines' rather than exact string matching. Section 4.2 explicitly states 'do not use snapshot testing'.

Provides a highly structured JSON test case format with fields: id, name, category, input, context (system_prompt, knowledge_base, conversation_history), expected_behavior (general, output_properties), scoring_weights, pass_threshold, and tags. 35 test cases provided across 4 categories.

Section 5 provides an evaluation report template with scoring summary table (dimension, mean, std, pass rate, thresholds), failure analysis template with checklist format for hallucination types and coherence issues, and optimization suggestions prioritized by severity.

Section 2.1 defines Hallucination Rate (HR) with formula, severity levels (Critical/Moderate/Minor with weights), Weighted Hallucination Score (WHS), Groundedness Score (GS), and Refusal Appropriateness Rate (RAR).

Section 2.2 defines context retention metrics: Context Recall Rate (CRR), Context Consistency Score (CCS), Entity Tracking Accuracy (ETA), and Instruction Persistence Rate (IPR) - all measuring multi-turn coherence.

Section 3.3 states 'Run each test case multiple times because LLM outputs are non-deterministic. Use temperature=0 for lower variance but still run 3-5 times to capture stochastic behavior.' Dataset recommendations show 3-5 runs per case.

Uses LLM-as-judge approach with claim extraction and classification (SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED/UNSUPPORTED) rather than exact string matching. Section 4.2 provides rule-based behavioral checks (entity tracking, forbidden phrases).

Section 3.2 provides a YAML test case schema with test_case_id, category, scenario, user_messages (turn-by-turn), ground_truth (knowledge_base, relevant_facts with sources, expected_claims, hallucination_triggers, expected_behavior), and metadata.

Section 10 provides a detailed per-run summary report template with hallucination metrics table, context retention metrics table, severity breakdown, top hallucination patterns, context loss by distance, composite quality score, and prioritized recommendations.
